messages:
alex_chang: Heads-up — ran a cross-device kernel pass comparing L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100 for seqlen distributions we see in chat workloads. Notable divergence around short tail (<=64) and long tail (>=2048).
marta_velasquez: nice, what stands out? :eyes:
alex_chang: L4/T4/A10: our cheap-allocator kernel (workspace-constrained) does well for seqlen<=64 but drops to a fallback GEMM path at ~512+ causing 2.2-3x latency increase. A100/H100 pick fused-attn kernels that stay stable out to 2048.
kevin_liu: is that the alloc size or a kernel autotuner mispick? do we have the kernel selection logs?
irene: autotuner log shows decision reason: `workspace_unavailable -> fallback` for L4/T4/A10 on many tokens. we set `kernel_policy=cost+mem` in the run.
perf-bot: profile summary (1876543300): device=L4, model=redwood-7b, batch=8, seq=1024, p50=95ms, p95=260ms, perf_regression=+180% vs baseline(A100)
alex_chang: attaching a quick config snippet I tested locally:
```
runtime:
  kernel_policy: cost+mem
  kv_prefetch: true
  max_workspace_mb: 1024  # L4 constrained
  seq_histogram: [0-64:0.6,65-512:0.3,513+:0.1]
```
marta_velasquez: kv_prefetch true + small workspace = interesting. do we see any KV-cache thrashing? that could explain stalls on long sequences.
kevin_liu: yes, logs show repeated cache rebuilds when user seq spikes. our prefix/KV reuse heuristics expect stable prefix lengths; when it flips from 32->2048 we rebuild and reallocate which kills throughput.
irene: suggestion: add a device-tiered kernel candidate list and a sequence-aware warmup policy. e.g., for L4/T4/A10 have a 'fast-short' path and a 'graceful-long' path that preallocs a minimal KV slab when seq_histogram.high > 0.05.
alex_chang: also thinking of a cheap autotune pass at startup for devices with small workspace: run 3 short microbenchmarks at seqlen {32,256,1024} to populate kernel score table. takes ~2s and avoids worst mispicks.
perf-bot: quick microbench sim (1876543500): L4 autoselect before microbench p95=270ms, after microbench p95=130ms (seq=1024), cost +50% CPU but lowers latency.
marta_velasquez: sounds promising. small ask: capture the autotuner picks in traces (tag selected_kernel) so console can surface problematic fallbacks.
kevin_liu: agreed. action items: (1) implement microbench step + score persist (2) add `seq_sensitive_warmup` flag (default off) (3) emit trace tags for kernel pick reasons.
irene: I'll draft a short patch for the kernel selector logic and the trace tag schema. will post a PR later today.
alex_chang: perfect. if we can avoid the fallback GEMM on L4/T4/A10 we'll get 30-60% p95 wins for medium-long chat loads. :thumbsup:
